title: ETS2: do we know what we want to measure and achieve?
text: From 2028 the European Union will put a price on CO₂ emissions from heating buildings and from motor fuels. The new emissions trading system, ETS2, was originally due to start in 2027, but this year the EU postponed it by a year1, and Czechia and Italy are now pushing for it to be suspended2. If ETS2 does go ahead, the state will earn new revenue from selling allowances, which it must spend on climate and social measures3. Before we decide what to do with that money, we should be clear about two things: what we want to achieve, and how we will know that we have achieved it.

title: ETS2: do we know what we want to measure and achieve?
section: Europe pays more and regulates more
text:
Europe pays more and regulates more
Reducing CO₂ emissions is, in general, a sensible goal. But Europe is not alone on this path, and it should pay close attention to how its main rivals see it. Since January 2026 the United States has not been a party to the Paris Agreement4, and the US government has declared a “national energy emergency” to expand domestic energy production, including oil and natural gas5. China has extended its emissions trading system to steel, cement and aluminium, but for now it regulates only emissions per unit of output, not their total amount. It plans to introduce absolute caps gradually from 20276.
European firms, meanwhile, pay far more for energy than their competitors. The 2024 Draghi report on the future of European competitiveness states that EU companies pay two to three times more for electricity than companies in the US, and four to five times more for natural gas. It names Europe’s lack of natural resources as the main cause, but also flaws in the common energy market and high taxes. And it warns that if Europe fails to coordinate its policies, decarbonisation risks running contrary to competitiveness and growth7.
The second problem is regulation. According to the same report, more than 60% of EU companies see it as an obstacle to investment, and 55% of small and medium-sized enterprises name regulatory obstacles and administrative burden as their greatest challenge8. Between 2019 and 2024 the EU passed around 13,000 acts, while around 3,500 laws and 2,000 resolutions were adopted at federal level in the US9. Draghi also points out that the EU has no common methodology for measuring the cost of regulation10. A reliable overall figure for how much regulation adds to the price of European products is therefore missing. Partial estimates do exist: according to a study for the European Commission, EU legislation from 2004 to 2014 cost the chemical industry about 12% of its value added and as much as 30% of its gross operating surplus, roughly its profit11. The Commission itself aims to cut firms’ recurring administrative costs by €37.5 billion a year by 202912.
Part of the problem, however, is at home. In October this year the President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, proposed a “pact against overregulation”: member states should show which obligations come from EU law and which they have added themselves13. Czechia has improved as far as new laws are concerned. Since 2016 a government methodology has required directives to be transposed in their minimal form and any additional requirement to be justified. Unjustified gold-plating has since almost disappeared from new legislation14. It persists, however, in older laws, in MPs’ amendments and in practice15. For example, when a building that was built and last substantially altered before 1947 is sold or let, no energy performance certificate is needed if both parties agree in writing16. According to an analysis by the Association for International Affairs (AMO), however, the media and firms that prepare such assessments often keep quiet about exemptions of this kind17. Exemptions that spare people administrative burden are welcome; people must, however, be made aware of them. According to the Czech Chamber of Commerce, administration costs Czech businesses around CZK 72 billion a year, and the government wants to cut this by a fifth by 202918.
At the same time, Europe has few fossil resources of its own19. In 2024 it imported 57% of the energy available to it, and two thirds of these imports were oil and petroleum products20. Reducing dependence on imported fossil fuels is therefore the right thing to do regardless of the climate.

title: ETS2: do we know what we want to measure and achieve?
section: What the indicators see and what they miss
text:
What the indicators see and what they miss
The rules for ETS2 money have two parts. Revenue from some of the allowances goes to the Social Climate Fund, which has at most €65 billion available for 2026 to 203221; Czechia can receive up to CZK 50 billion from it22. The state must add at least 25% of the costs of its Social Climate Plan23. At most 37.5% of these costs may go to temporary direct income support for households, so most of the money must go to measures with a lasting effect, such as building renovation, clean heating or zero-emission transport24. The state keeps the remaining ETS2 revenue and must use it for climate purposes, giving priority to social impacts25. Moreover, the Commission pays out money from the Fund only if the state meets the targets of its plan, and these must include a reduction in the number of households in energy poverty26.
We calculated the impact of ETS2 on Czech households with a model that links two levels. The macroeconomic model E3ME calculates how ETS2 changes prices and incomes across the whole economy, and the dynamic microsimulation DASMOD carries these changes through to the budgets of 3,233 households from household surveys, which represent 4.62 million Czech households. Unlike static estimates, which simply apply higher prices to today’s consumption, households in the model respond to changes in prices and incomes in the way the data on their spending show. The model also tracks their savings and debts, so it captures how a renovation is financed, and for every result we report how precisely the data can measure it27. The main finding is that what energy poverty indicators record depends as much on how they are constructed as on the policy itself28.
In our scenario, the average Czech household will pay €218 a year more for energy in 2032 because of ETS2, or 0.73% of its net income. Households heating with gas and pensioners living alone will be hit hardest29. We compared what happens when the same €745 million over 2028 to 2032 goes to insulation and heat pumps and, for comparison, to direct payments to households30. A direct payment brings people relief, but an indicator that judges high energy costs by the level of spending reads the part of the money spent on heating as a deterioration, so 87% of the relief disappears from it31. The official indicators move by only fractions of a percentage point32. Insulation and heat pumps reduce energy poverty, as measured by indicators that combine low income and high costs, by 7.1 to 10.5%, and three years after the programme ends the reduction is still at least 5.4%33.
The result also depends on how a renovation is paid for. An indicator that tracks a household’s savings as well as its income and costs records whether the household paid its co-payment from savings or with a loan. If it draws on its savings, the indicator counts this as a deterioration: for a heat pump, the fall in savings wipes out 36% of the improvement brought by lower bills. Conversely, the saved part of a direct payment shows up in it as relief34. The same renovation can therefore come out better or worse simply depending on how it was paid for. Goals and measurement rules need to be set before the money starts to flow, and instead of a single number we should track several indicators, each with its precision35.

title: ETS2: do we know what we want to measure and achieve?
section: ETS2 revenue for a more resilient economy
text:
ETS2 revenue for a more resilient economy
The revenue the state keeps from ETS2 may already be used, among other things, for renewable energy, transmission grids and other technologies that contribute to the transition to a safe and sustainable low-carbon economy36. These provisions do not mention nuclear power explicitly. Revenue from the existing allowance system for industry and power generation, ETS1, has gone mainly to the State Environmental Fund since this year. According to the Ministry of the Environment, it is to finance, for example, new renewable sources, the modernisation of heating plants, energy savings in businesses and buildings, and support for low- and middle-income households37. I would apply the same logic to ETS2, and more boldly. Most of the money from allowances should strengthen the resilience of the economy as a whole, that is, finance our own energy sources, both nuclear and renewable, and the grids that connect them. A smaller part should go to targeted support for the households hit hardest by ETS2. The Draghi report, too, counts on both kinds of sources with low running costs38.
China shows that this can be done on a large scale: it is investing massively in renewables. In 2025 alone, according to the International Energy Agency, it added almost 500 gigawatts of renewable capacity, more than 60% of global growth, including nearly 370 GW of solar and 117 GW of wind39.
Such investments are expensive. For the two new units at Dukovany the state will pay the Korean company KHNP CZK 407 billion at current prices40. Construction is to be covered by a state loan, which the European Commission estimates at €23 to 30 billion and has been examining in depth since December 202541. In August this year the Minister of Industry, Karel Havlíček, acknowledged that, including the cost of money, the two units will cost CZK 600 to 700 billion42.

title: ETS2: do we know what we want to measure and achieve?
text:
What mix makes sense
In my view, the ideal mix should ease the regulations that make products unnecessarily expensive, in Brussels and at home. The state should serve citizens and businesses, not the other way round: if it needs certain data, it should obtain them itself rather than shifting that obligation onto households and firms. At the same time, we need to reduce our dependence on imported fossil fuels for good. ETS2 revenue should go mainly into our own energy sources and infrastructure. The households hit hardest by ETS2 need targeted help, ideally of a kind that lowers their bills permanently.
So what is the answer to the question we started with? We should aim for greater self-sufficiency in energy. And we will know we have succeeded when price swings on world markets feed through to household bills only very slightly.

      Bridging the Gap: A Novel M2/LIHC Hybrid Indicator Unveils Energy Poverty Dynamics – Case Study of the Czech Republic
      Spoluautoři: Milan Ščasný
      IES Working Papers č. 6/2025
      
        
        
        
        
          Abstrakt
          This paper introduces a novel composite energy poverty indicator, the M2LIHC, which combines elements of the twice-median expenditure share (2M) and Low Income High Cost (LIHC) measures. Using a unique dataset merging the Czech Household Budget Survey and EU-SILC data from 2017-2022, we demonstrate how this hybrid approach provides new insights into energy poverty dynamics. The M2LIHC indicator addresses key limitations of existing metrics, avoiding the LIHC measure’s counterintuitive response to income changes in the lowest decile and mitigating the 2M indicator’s potential overestimation of energy poverty among higher-income households with high energy costs. Our comparative analysis reveals significant differences in energy poverty rates and household characteristics identified by each indicator. The M2LIHC measure proves more robust to income fluctuations than LIHC while maintaining sensitivity to both income and energy cost components. We find energy poverty in the Czech Republic has increased across all indicators from 2017 to 2022, with the M2LIHC indicator suggesting a rise from 8.9% to 13.5%. To further validate our approach, we employ the DASMOD (Distributional And Social Impact Model) to simulate various energy and climate policy scenarios. These simulations demonstrate the complex effects of compensation policies on energy poverty measures, with M2LIHC providing a more nuanced view of policy impacts. By providing a more comprehensive and theoretically consistent measure of energy poverty, coupled with policy simulation capabilities, the M2LIHC indicator offers policymakers an improved tool for targeting support and assessing the effectiveness of energy poverty alleviation strategies in the context of energy transitions and climate policies.

      Publication Bias and Model Uncertainty in Measuring the Effect of Class Size on Achievement
      Spoluautoři: Tomáš Havránek, Zuzana Irsova a Milan Ščasný
      Journal of Labor Economics V tisku
      
        DOI
        
        
        
          Abstrakt
          Class size reduction mandates are routinely justified by studies reporting positive effects on student achievement. Yet other studies report no effects, and the literature as a whole awaits correction for potential publication bias. Moreover, if identification drives results systematically, the relevance of individual studies will vary. We build a sample of 2,819 estimates collected from 66 studies and for each estimate classify 42 factors that reflect estimation context. We employ nonlinear techniques for publication bias correction and model averaging techniques to address model uncertainty. The results are consistent with little publication bias. The implied class size effect is negligible for all identification approaches except Tennessee’s Student/Teacher Achievement Ratio project and for all contexts except classes of fewer than 15 students.

      Spoluautoři: Milan Ščasný
      The Journal of Economic Inequality, 24(1), 261–281

          Abstrakt
          We provide the first estimate of the elasticity of marginal utility of consumption, μ, for a post-transition economy in the Central & Eastern European region – the Czech Republic – based on household-level data. Using the absolute equal-sacrifice income tax approach, we obtain a central estimate of μ at 1.47, which varies between 1.32 to 1.66 within the study period covering 2005–2022. Moreover, the estimate of the elasticity of marginal utility of consumption differs between various income groups, indicating that this approach is suitable only for those who pay income tax. Including the non-taxpayers segment means ceteris paribus negative μ, and hence its smaller value for the entire population. Importantly, the μ estimate increases when social benefits are included in gross income, and it decreases when social and health insurance contributions are included in the definition of taxes. Since parameter μ is a crucial component of the social discount rate, our result provides useful input for policies that affect intertemporal allocations.

      Volumetric choice experiments and welfare measures in a subsidy-driven context
      Spoluautoři: Wiktor Budziński, Mikołaj Czajkowski a dalších 10
      Resource and Energy Economics, 86, článek 101572
      
        DOI
        
        
        
          Abstrakt
          Volumetric Choice Experiments (VCE) offer a novel approach to studying individual behavior, traditionally explored through Discrete Choice Experiments. This study assesses the efficacy of VCE in understanding farmers' preferences regarding new results-based and practice-based agri-environmental contracts, using a comprehensive international stated preference survey. Recognizing that farmers often act as households maximizing utility rather than purely profit-driven producers, we provide justification for applying a utility-based framework in this context. The subsidy-driven nature of agri-environmental contracts poses a challenge for the use of multiple discrete-continuous choice models suited for VCE data. Conventionally, these models utilize an income-based budget equation, which would not be binding given the willingness-to-accept format of the experiment. To operationalize our model, we adopt a land-based budget equation, facilitating the development of a novel compensating variation measure for welfare analysis. Our findings reveal insightful contrasts between VCE-derived data and traditional DCE results, highlighting the complexities encountered and the comparability of outcomes. By delving into the distinct attributes of VCE and justifying the utility-based approach for farmers, this research not only bridges a critical gap in the literature but also enhances our understanding of farmer behavior, with significant implications for the design and implementation of future agri-environmental policies.

        DOI
        
        
        
          Abstrakt
          Over the past several decades, meta-analysis has emerged as a widely accepted tool to understand economics research. Meta-analyses often challenge the established conventional wisdom of their respective fields. We systematically review a wide range of influential meta-analyses in economics and compare them to “conventional wisdom.” After correcting for observable biases, the empirical economic effects are typically much closer to zero and sometimes switch signs.           We estimate how the UK financial markets would have evolved if the Remain camp had won the referendum. To construct the counterfactual, we use the synthetic control method.           Czech farmers experienced an enormous exogenous shock when they joined the common agricultural market (CAM) and the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) in 2004.           Abstrakt
          In this paper I evaluate the quantitative effects of the Czech National Bank's commitment to keep the Koruna from appreciating that were put in place in 2013. I focus on the policy's impact on output, unemployment, and inflation. I use the synthetic control method, which allows me to compute the counter-factual development of the Czech economy in the absence of the commitment. title: ETS2: víme, co chceme měřit a čeho dosáhnout?
text: Od roku 2028 začne Evropská unie zpoplatňovat emise CO₂ z vytápění budov a z pohonných hmot. Nový systém emisních povolenek ETS2 měl startovat už v roce 2027, EU ho ale letos o rok odložila1 a Česko s Itálií teď prosazují jeho pozastavení2. Pokud ETS2 začne platit, získá stát z prodeje povolenek nové příjmy, které musí použít na klimatická a sociální opatření3. Než rozhodneme, co s nimi, měli bychom mít jasno ve dvou věcech: čeho chceme dosáhnout a podle čeho poznáme, že se to povedlo.

title: ETS2: víme, co chceme měřit a čeho dosáhnout?
section: Evropa platí víc a reguluje víc
text:
Evropa platí víc a reguluje víc
Snižovat emise CO₂ je obecně rozumný cíl. Evropa na této cestě ale není sama a měla by pozorně sledovat, jak ji vidí její hlavní rivalové. Spojené státy od ledna 2026 nejsou součástí Pařížské dohody4 a americká vláda vyhlásila „národní energetickou nouzi“, aby rozšířila domácí těžbu a výrobu energie včetně ropy a zemního plynu5. Čína sice rozšířila svůj trh s povolenkami na ocel, cement a hliník, zatím ale reguluje jen emise na jednotku výroby, ne jejich celkové množství. Pevné stropy chce zavádět postupně od roku 20276.
Evropské firmy přitom za energii platí mnohem víc než jejich konkurenti. Draghiho zpráva o budoucnosti evropské konkurenceschopnosti z roku 2024 uvádí, že firmy v EU platí za elektřinu dvakrát až třikrát víc než v USA a za zemní plyn čtyřikrát až pětkrát víc. Za hlavní příčinu označuje nedostatek vlastních přírodních zdrojů, ale také vady společného trhu s energií a vysoké daně. A varuje, že pokud Evropa své politiky nesladí, hrozí, že dekarbonizace půjde proti konkurenceschopnosti a růstu7.
Druhým problémem je regulace. Podle téže zprávy ji více než 60 % firem v EU považuje za překážku investic a 55 % malých a středních podniků označuje regulatorní překážky a administrativu za svůj největší problém8. V letech 2019 až 2024 přijala EU zhruba 13 tisíc aktů, zatímco v USA vzniklo na federální úrovni asi 3 500 zákonů a 2 000 rezolucí9. Draghi zároveň upozorňuje, že EU nemá společnou metodiku, jak náklady regulace měřit10. Spolehlivé souhrnné číslo o tom, o kolik regulace zdražuje evropské výrobky, proto chybí. Dílčí odhady ano: podle studie pro Evropskou komisi stála legislativa EU z let 2004 až 2014 chemický průmysl zhruba 12 % jeho přidané hodnoty a až 30 % hrubého provozního přebytku, tedy přibližně zisku11. Sama Komise si dala za cíl snížit opakované administrativní náklady firem do roku 2029 o 37,5 miliardy eur ročně12.
Část problému je ale doma. Předsedkyně Evropské komise Ursula von der Leyenová letos v říjnu navrhla „pakt proti nadměrné regulaci“: členské státy by měly ukázat, které povinnosti pocházejí z práva EU a které si přidaly samy13. U nových zákonů se Česko zlepšilo. Od roku 2016 platí vládní metodika, podle níž se směrnice přebírají v minimální podobě a každé přitvrzení je třeba zdůvodnit. Neodůvodněné přitvrzování z nových zákonů od té doby téměř zmizelo14. Zůstává ale ve starších předpisech, v poslaneckých pozměňovacích návrzích a v praxi15. Například při prodeji nebo pronájmu budovy postavené a naposledy větší měrou upravené před rokem 1947 se průkaz energetické náročnosti nemusí pořizovat, pokud se na tom obě strany písemně dohodnou16. Podle analýzy AMO ale média a firmy zpracovávající posudky takové výjimky často zamlčují17. Výjimky, které lidem ušetří administrativu, jsou správné; lidé se o nich však musí dozvědět. Administrativa podle Hospodářské komory stojí české podnikatele zhruba 72 miliard korun ročně a vláda ji chce do roku 2029 snížit o pětinu18.
Zároveň platí, že vlastních fosilních zdrojů má Evropa málo19. V roce 2024 dovezla 57 % energie, kterou měla k dispozici, a dvě třetiny dovozu tvořila ropa a ropné produkty20. Snižovat závislost na dovozu fosilních paliv je proto správné i bez ohledu na klima.

title: ETS2: víme, co chceme měřit a čeho dosáhnout?
section: Co ukazatele uvidí a co ne
text:
Co ukazatele uvidí a co ne
Pravidla pro peníze z ETS2 mají dvě části. Výnos z části povolenek jde do Sociálního klimatického fondu, který má na roky 2026 až 2032 k dispozici nejvýše 65 miliard eur21; Česko z něj může získat až 50 miliard korun22. Stát k tomu musí přidat nejméně 25 % nákladů svého Sociálního klimatického plánu23. Na dočasnou přímou podporu příjmů domácností smí jít nejvýše 37,5 % těchto nákladů, většina tedy musí jít do opatření s trvalým účinkem, jako jsou renovace budov, čisté vytápění nebo bezemisní doprava24. Zbývající výnosy z ETS2 si stát ponechá a musí je použít na klimatické účely, přednostně s ohledem na sociální dopady25. Komise přitom peníze z fondu vyplácí, jen pokud stát plní cíle svého plánu, a mezi nimi musí být i snížení počtu domácností v energetické chudobě26.
Dopady ETS2 na české domácnosti jsme spočítali v modelu, který propojuje dvě úrovně. Makroekonomický model E3ME počítá, jak ETS2 změní ceny a příjmy v celé ekonomice, a dynamická mikrosimulace DASMOD tyto změny promítá do rozpočtů 3 233 domácností z výběrových šetření, které zastupují 4,62 milionu českých domácností. Na rozdíl od statických odhadů, které vyšší ceny jen přepočítají na dnešní spotřebu, domácnosti v modelu na změny cen a příjmů reagují tak, jak to ukazují data o jejich výdajích. Model sleduje i jejich úspory a dluhy, takže zachytí, jak se renovace financuje, a u každého výsledku uvádíme, jak přesně ho data dokážou změřit27. Hlavní zjištění zní: to, co ukazatele energetické chudoby zaznamenají, závisí na jejich konstrukci stejně jako na samotné politice28.
V našem scénáři zaplatí průměrná česká domácnost v roce 2032 kvůli ETS2 za energie o 218 eur ročně víc, tedy 0,73 % čistého příjmu. Nejvíc to zasáhne domácnosti, které topí plynem, a osaměle žijící důchodce29. Porovnali jsme, co se stane, když stejných 745 milionů eur v letech 2028 až 2032 půjde na zateplení a tepelná čerpadla, a pro srovnání i na přímé platby domácnostem30. Přímá platba lidem uleví, ale ukazatel, který vysoké náklady na energie posuzuje podle výše výdajů, si část peněz utracenou za teplo vyloží jako zhoršení, a 87 % úlevy v něm tak zmizí31. Oficiální ukazatele se pohnou jen o zlomky procentního bodu32. Zateplení a tepelná čerpadla snižují energetickou chudobu měřenou ukazateli, které kombinují nízký příjem a vysoké náklady, o 7,1 až 10,5 % a ještě tři roky po skončení programu je pokles nejméně 5,4 %33.
Výsledek ovlivňuje i to, jak se renovace zaplatí. Ukazatel, který vedle příjmu a nákladů sleduje i úspory domácnosti, zaznamená, zda domácnost zaplatila spoluúčast z úspor, nebo z půjčky. Když sáhne do úspor, ukazatel to vyhodnotí jako zhoršení: u tepelného čerpadla tak úbytek úspor smaže 36 % zlepšení, které přinesly nižší účty. Uspořená část přímé platby se v něm naopak projeví jako úleva34. Stejná renovace tak může vyjít lépe nebo hůř jen podle toho, jak byla zaplacena. Cíle a pravidla měření je proto potřeba stanovit dřív, než peníze začnou proudit, a místo jednoho čísla sledovat několik ukazatelů, každý i s jeho přesností35.

title: ETS2: víme, co chceme měřit a čeho dosáhnout?
section: Výnosy z ETS2 do odolnosti ekonomiky
text:
Výnosy z ETS2 do odolnosti ekonomiky
Výnosy, které si stát z ETS2 ponechá, smí už dnes jít mimo jiné na obnovitelné zdroje, přenosové sítě a další technologie přispívající k přechodu na bezpečnou a udržitelnou nízkouhlíkovou ekonomiku36. Jaderné zdroje tato ustanovení výslovně nezmiňují. Výnosy ze stávajícího systému povolenek pro průmysl a energetiku, ETS1, jdou od letošního roku převážně do Státního fondu životního prostředí. Podle ministerstva mají financovat například nové obnovitelné zdroje, modernizaci tepláren, úspory energie v podnicích a budovách i podporu domácností s nižšími a středními příjmy37. Stejnou logiku bych uplatnil i u ETS2, a to odvážněji. Většina peněz z povolenek by měla posilovat odolnost ekonomiky jako celku, tedy financovat vlastní zdroje energie, jaderné i obnovitelné, a sítě, které je propojí. Menší část by měla jít na cílenou pomoc domácnostem, které ETS2 zasáhne nejvíc. S oběma druhy zdrojů s nízkými provozními náklady počítá i Draghiho zpráva38.
Že se to dá dělat ve velkém, ukazuje Čína, která do obnovitelných zdrojů investuje masivně. Jen v roce 2025 v ní podle Mezinárodní energetické agentury přibylo téměř 500 gigawattů obnovitelných zdrojů, přes 60 % celosvětového přírůstku, z toho téměř 370 GW solárních a 117 GW větrných elektráren39.
Takové investice jsou drahé. Za dva nové bloky v Dukovanech zaplatí stát korejské firmě KHNP 407 miliard korun v současných cenách40. Stavbu má pokrýt státní půjčka, kterou Evropská komise odhaduje na 23 až 30 miliard eur a od prosince 2025 ji podrobně prověřuje41. Ministr průmyslu Karel Havlíček letos v srpnu připustil, že s cenou peněz vyjdou oba bloky na 600 až 700 miliard korun42.

title: ETS2: víme, co chceme měřit a čeho dosáhnout?
text:
Jaký mix dává smysl
Ideální mix by podle mě měl uvolnit regulace, které výrobky zbytečně zdražují, v Bruselu i doma. Stát by měl sloužit občanům a firmám, nikoli naopak: pokud potřebuje určité údaje, měl by si je opatřit sám, a nepřenášet tuto povinnost na domácnosti a podniky. Zároveň je potřeba trvale snižovat závislost na dovozu fosilních paliv. Výnosy z ETS2 by měly jít hlavně do vlastních zdrojů energie a infrastruktury. Domácnosti, které ETS2 zasáhne nejvíc, potřebují cílenou pomoc, nejlépe takovou, která jim natrvalo sníží účty.
A odpověď na otázku z úvodu? Dosáhnout bychom měli větší soběstačnosti v energetických zdrojích. A že se to povedlo, poznáme podle toho, že se výkyvy cen na světových burzách promítnou do účtů domácností jen velmi málo.

      Bridging the Gap: A Novel M2/LIHC Hybrid Indicator Unveils Energy Poverty Dynamics – Case Study of the Czech Republic
      with Milan Ščasný
      IES Working Papers No. 6/2025
      
        
        
        
        
          Abstract
          This paper introduces a novel composite energy poverty indicator, the M2LIHC, which combines elements of the twice-median expenditure share (2M) and Low Income High Cost (LIHC) measures. Using a unique dataset merging the Czech Household Budget Survey and EU-SILC data from 2017-2022, we demonstrate how this hybrid approach provides new insights into energy poverty dynamics. The M2LIHC indicator addresses key limitations of existing metrics, avoiding the LIHC measure’s counterintuitive response to income changes in the lowest decile and mitigating the 2M indicator’s potential overestimation of energy poverty among higher-income households with high energy costs. Our comparative analysis reveals significant differences in energy poverty rates and household characteristics identified by each indicator. The M2LIHC measure proves more robust to income fluctuations than LIHC while maintaining sensitivity to both income and energy cost components. We find energy poverty in the Czech Republic has increased across all indicators from 2017 to 2022, with the M2LIHC indicator suggesting a rise from 8.9% to 13.5%. To further validate our approach, we employ the DASMOD (Distributional And Social Impact Model) to simulate various energy and climate policy scenarios. These simulations demonstrate the complex effects of compensation policies on energy poverty measures, with M2LIHC providing a more nuanced view of policy impacts. By providing a more comprehensive and theoretically consistent measure of energy poverty, coupled with policy simulation capabilities, the M2LIHC indicator offers policymakers an improved tool for targeting support and assessing the effectiveness of energy poverty alleviation strategies in the context of energy transitions and climate policies.

      Publication Bias and Model Uncertainty in Measuring the Effect of Class Size on Achievement
      with Tomáš Havránek, Zuzana Irsova and Milan Ščasný
      Journal of Labor Economics Forthcoming
      
        DOI
        
        
        
          Abstract
          Class size reduction mandates are routinely justified by studies reporting positive effects on student achievement. Yet other studies report no effects, and the literature as a whole awaits correction for potential publication bias. Moreover, if identification drives results systematically, the relevance of individual studies will vary. We build a sample of 2,819 estimates collected from 66 studies and for each estimate classify 42 factors that reflect estimation context. We employ nonlinear techniques for publication bias correction and model averaging techniques to address model uncertainty. The results are consistent with little publication bias. The implied class size effect is negligible for all identification approaches except Tennessee’s Student/Teacher Achievement Ratio project and for all contexts except classes of fewer than 15 students.

      Elasticity of marginal utility of consumption: the equal-sacrifice approach applied for the Czech Republic
      with Milan Ščasný
      The Journal of Economic Inequality, 24(1), 261–281
      
        DOI
        
        
        
          Abstract
          We provide the first estimate of the elasticity of marginal utility of consumption, μ, for a post-transition economy in the Central & Eastern European region – the Czech Republic – based on household-level data. Using the absolute equal-sacrifice income tax approach, we obtain a central estimate of μ at 1.47, which varies between 1.32 to 1.66 within the study period covering 2005–2022. Moreover, the estimate of the elasticity of marginal utility of consumption differs between various income groups, indicating that this approach is suitable only for those who pay income tax. Including the non-taxpayers segment means ceteris paribus negative μ, and hence its smaller value for the entire population. Importantly, the μ estimate increases when social benefits are included in gross income, and it decreases when social and health insurance contributions are included in the definition of taxes. Since parameter μ is a crucial component of the social discount rate, our result provides useful input for policies that affect intertemporal allocations.

          Abstract
          We estimate the elasticity of marginal utility of consumption (μ) for Europe and 32 individual European countries using household-level income tax data.       Reporting Guidelines for Meta-Analysis in Economics—Updated for AI

      Journal of Economic Surveys
      
        DOI
        
        
        
          Abstract
          Meta-analysis is how science takes stock of its vast research output. The advent of increasingly capable artificial intelligence (AI) promises an unprecedented ability to identify and synthesize relevant research and its findings. In this document, the meta-analysis of economics research network (MAER-Net) updates existing Reporting Guidelines to be consistent with community-driven best practices for the responsible use and disclosure of AI-assistance in meta-analysis research. This update is meant to further improve the transparency, replicability, and quality of meta-analyses by building upon the 2020 and 2013 Reporting Guidelines published by this Journal. Cook et al. Future meta-analyses, whether or not they use AI, are expected to follow these updated guidelines or to be prepared to give reasons if they deviate from them.

      Volumetric choice experiments and welfare measures in a subsidy-driven context
      with Wiktor Budziński, Mikołaj Czajkowski and 10 others
      Resource and Energy Economics, 86, Article 101572
      
        DOI
        
        
        
          Abstract
          Volumetric Choice Experiments (VCE) offer a novel approach to studying individual behavior, traditionally explored through Discrete Choice Experiments. This study assesses the efficacy of VCE in understanding farmers' preferences regarding new results-based and practice-based agri-environmental contracts, using a comprehensive international stated preference survey. Recognizing that farmers often act as households maximizing utility rather than purely profit-driven producers, we provide justification for applying a utility-based framework in this context. The subsidy-driven nature of agri-environmental contracts poses a challenge for the use of multiple discrete-continuous choice models suited for VCE data. Conventionally, these models utilize an income-based budget equation, which would not be binding given the willingness-to-accept format of the experiment. To operationalize our model, we adopt a land-based budget equation, facilitating the development of a novel compensating variation measure for welfare analysis. Our findings reveal insightful contrasts between VCE-derived data and traditional DCE results, highlighting the complexities encountered and the comparability of outcomes. By delving into the distinct attributes of VCE and justifying the utility-based approach for farmers, this research not only bridges a critical gap in the literature but also enhances our understanding of farmer behavior, with significant implications for the design and implementation of future agri-environmental policies.

      Conventional wisdom, meta-analysis, and research revision in economics
      with Sebastian Gechert, Bianka Mey and 7 others
      Journal of Economic Surveys, 39(3), 980–999
      
        DOI
        
        
        
          Abstract
          Over the past several decades, meta-analysis has emerged as a widely accepted tool to understand economics research. Meta-analyses often challenge the established conventional wisdom of their respective fields. We systematically review a wide range of influential meta-analyses in economics and compare them to “conventional wisdom.” After correcting for observable biases, the empirical economic effects are typically much closer to zero and sometimes switch signs. Typically, the relative reduction in effect sizes is 45%–60%.

      The impact of the Brexit vote on UK financial markets: a synthetic control method approach
      
      Empirica, 48(2), 559–587
      
        DOI
        
        
        
          Abstract
          We estimate how the UK financial markets would have evolved if the Remain camp had won the referendum. To construct the counterfactual, we use the synthetic control method. Our results suggest that there would not have been any significant change in the development of the FTSE 100 Index in the medium to long term if there had not been a referendum. On the other hand, we find a significantly negative effect of 1.2 percentage points on the 10-year bond yield. Given the geopolitical circumstances in mid 2016, financial agents investing in the pound could have sought safer investment options represented by longer-term government bonds, which consequently could result in lower bond yields.

          Abstract
          Czech farmers experienced an enormous exogenous shock when they joined the common agricultural market (CAM) and the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) in 2004. Using the World Bank's dataset, we apply the synthetic control method to establish a counterfactual case of the Czech Republic food production index in the absence of the CAM and CAP. The results show that the Czech Republic would have had a higher food index if it had not entered the CAM and CAP. Moreover, we show that the CAP and CAM had different impacts on farms in the Czech Republic and Bulgaria, which have the most comparable agriculture according to the results of the synthetic control method.

          Abstract
          In this paper I evaluate the quantitative effects of the Czech National Bank's commitment to keep the Koruna from appreciating that were put in place in 2013. I focus on the policy's impact on output, unemployment, and inflation. I use the synthetic control method, which allows me to compute the counter-factual development of the Czech economy in the absence of the commitment. I find that the commitment helped decrease unemployment substantially. The effect on overall output is also strongly positive, almost 2 percentage points for growth in 2015, but only marginally statistically significant, which might be connected to disturbances created by changes in excise taxes. The effect of the commitment on inflation is positive but not statistically significant at standard levels.
